template.name: The Oath-Breaker's Rite

steps.narrativeTemplate:
{cast:oathbreaker}, a weaver, broke an oath sworn on the stone in the town shrine. Since then the weaver's workshop has burned. The shrine lamp goes out whenever the weaver walks in.

{cast:oathbreaker} is sure of a curse and asks {actor}, a reader of oaths, whether it is real. A frightened hedge-priest has already taken the weaver's coin for a rite at midnight. A wrong answer will cost {actor} their name in town.
steps.criticalSuccessAfterimage: They read the stone plainly. The oath was a promise to repay a neighbour's loan by midsummer, and it still holds; that is why the lamp goes out. No curse follows the weaver. The fire was the weaver's own lamp, left burning.
steps.successAfterimage: They found the oath still holding on the stone, and no curse on the weaver at all.
steps.successAtCostAfterimage: They found the oath still holding and no curse, after a reading so slow that the weaver nearly left.
steps.failureAfterimage: They felt the oath's weight at the stone, and could not tell it from a curse.
steps.criticalFailureAfterimage: They told the weaver the curse was real.

nudges.name: Remember The Old Ways
nudges.effectLine: Bring the oath-rite back to their mind as it was first done. They lean toward performing it at the stone.

bandProse.critical_success: The oath-rite came back to them whole, and they read the stone by it.
bandProse.success: The oath-rite came back to them, and the stone answered it.
bandProse.near_miss: Half of the oath-rite came back to them, and the stone answered half.
bandProse.failure: The oath-rite came back to them wrong, and they read the stone by a wrong verse.

nudges.name: Stir Doubt
nudges.effectLine: Make every rite they know sound hollow to them. They lean toward refusing every rite and telling the plain truth.

bandProse.success_at_cost: They doubted the stone out loud, and the weaver heard it.
bandProse.failure: They doubted the stone, and then doubted what it showed them.
bandProse.critical_failure: They doubted every true sign at the stone and trusted the one false sign.

positive.narrativeTemplate: {actor} offers the weaver the old rite in place of the priest's. The old rite is spoken at the stone, before witnesses. {cast:priest}, the hedge-priest, keeps the coin and holds a rival rite in the square. There the priest tells the crowd that the strangers camped outside the gate brought the curse. {actor} must loose the oath before the crowd believes the priest.
positive.criticalSuccessAfterimage: They loosed the oath in its first form, word for word.
positive.successAfterimage: They loosed the oath at the stone.
positive.successAtCostAfterimage: They loosed the oath, but the rite ran until dawn.
positive.failureAfterimage: The oath held against every verse they spoke.
positive.criticalFailureAfterimage: The oath held, and the shrine lamp went out in their hand.

critical_success.text: They know the oath holds and no curse does.

success.text: They know what holds the weaver.

success_at_cost.text: The weaver trusts their reading less.

near_miss.text: They know only part of the oath.

failure.text: They cannot tell the oath from a curse.

nudges.name: Twist The Words
nudges.effectLine: Make the hedge-priest stumble through the rival rite in the square, so the crowd drifts back toward the shrine.

bandProse.success: {cast:priest} lost the rival rite twice in the square, and the crowd walked back to the shrine.
bandProse.near_miss: {cast:priest} lost the rival rite once, and only half the crowd walked back.
bandProse.failure: {cast:priest} lost a verse and found it again, and the crowd stayed in the square.
bandProse.critical_failure: {cast:priest} spoke the rival rite without one slip, and the crowd stayed to hear it all.

nudges.name: Wake The Stone
nudges.effectLine: Stir the memory the shrine holds, so the oath answers the old rite more readily.

bandProse.critical_success: The stone answered the first verse, and the lamp above it flared and held.
bandProse.success: The stone answered the rite as it had answered the swearing.
bandProse.success_at_cost: The stone answered one verse at a time, and slowly.
bandProse.failure: The stone answered only with the oath, still owed.

negative.narrativeTemplate: {actor} refuses to hold any rite and tells the weaver to keep the oath instead. {cast:priest}, the hedge-priest, holds the midnight rite in the square anyway. The priest blames the strangers camped outside the gate. The crowd is afraid, and it would rather believe a priest than a doubter. {actor} must prove to the whole square that the priest's rite calls on no power.
negative.criticalSuccessAfterimage: They took the priest's rite apart in front of the square, step by step.
negative.successAfterimage: They showed the crowd that the priest's rite called on no power at all.
negative.successAtCostAfterimage: They turned the crowd, and lost the weaver.
negative.failureAfterimage: The crowd listened to the priest over them.
negative.criticalFailureAfterimage: The crowd turned on them as well as on the strangers.

template.description: An opt-in oath reading at a town shrine: read a broken oath on the shrine stone (Veil), then, by the mortal's own regard for old rites, loosen the oath by the old rite against a frightened hedge-priest's rival rite (Archivist, Veil) or refuse every rite and prove to the crowd in the square that the priest's rite is empty (Heretic, Veil). A true release tends the shrine; any failure lets the priest blame the strangers at the gate, and the town sets a watch.
